sources.title: Fan Li, STA610 Lecture 1 Notes: The Problem of Correlated Data
sources.locator: PDF pp. 4–8, §§2.3–2.5, for the random-intercept moment model and compound-symmetry covariance; pp. 8–9, §3.1, for the ICC. The complete 11-page note was inspected.
sources.reading_verification: Read the complete local extracted text at scratchpad/statistics-scaffolds-2026-10-11/sources/models-01/duke-sta610-lec1-correlated-data.txt. The source assumes Gaussian random intercepts and residuals for its model example; the local covariance lemma and ICC verification use only the stated first and second moments and independence.

contents.name: 2.3–2.5 Two-component random-intercept model, covariance derivation, and compound symmetry
contents.support: The source supplies the random-intercept decomposition and common-subject covariance pattern. The authored definition states the general vector moment model; the local covariance lemma proves its matrix formula without importing the source's Gaussian assumption.

contents.name: 2.4 From the model to a covariance
contents.support: The source expands the shared random-intercept and residual terms. The local proof gives the finite-dimensional matrix identity for arbitrary independent centered vectors.

contents.name: 3.1 Intraclass correlation
contents.support: The source identifies the ratio of between-subject variance to total variance as the common within-subject correlation; the example states and checks the positive-total-variance boundary.

contents.name: 1.1–1.4 Classical OLS assumptions and clustered standard-error consequences
contents.reason: This assigned pair develops GLS under a known covariance and mixed-model consequences; clustered robust standard errors and general OLS diagnostics are outside the SME-07 claim inventory.

sources.title: Fan Li, STA610 Lecture 2 Notes: Two Solutions—GLS and Cluster-Robust Standard Errors
sources.locator: PDF pp. 1–2, §1.1, for the general known-positive-definite-covariance whitening and GLS theorem; the complete 5-page note was inspected.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected all five PDF pages via the official Duke full-text PDF. The whitening proof and stated covariance/BLUE formula on pp. 1–2 were read in full. Sections 2.1–2.4 on robust standard errors were read and excluded from this pair.

contents.name: 1.1 Generalized least squares and Aitken’s theorem
contents.support: The source supplies the whitening route and general known-covariance formula. The authored proof applies the current fixed-design Gauss–Markov supplier and computes the covariance matrix directly.

contents.name: 1.2 Compound-symmetry specialization
contents.support: The source identifies GLS as the estimator for a specified positive-definite covariance; the item defines the known-V statistic and keeps estimated-V plug-in procedures separate.

contents.name: 2.1–2.4 Cluster-robust and heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors
contents.reason: Robust sandwich inference is a separate procedure and is not part of the assigned mixed-effects, known-covariance BLUE, or BLUP claims.

sources.title: Fan Li, STA610 Lecture 3 Notes: One-Way ANOVA and Random-Effects ANOVA
sources.locator: PDF pp. 4–6, §§2.2–2.4, for the random-effects moment model and conditional/marginal covariance distinction; the complete 9-page note was inspected.
sources.reading_verification: Read the complete local extracted text at scratchpad/statistics-scaffolds-2026-10-11/sources/models-01/duke-sta610-lec3-re-anova.txt. The note distinguishes fixed-effects tests from random-effects variance modeling; its balanced ANOVA moment estimators are not imported into SME-07.

contents.name: 2.2–2.4 Random-effects ANOVA and conditional versus marginal covariance
contents.support: The source independently derives the random-intercept marginal variance and same-subject covariance. The authored result generalizes this by a complete matrix proof.

contents.name: 3.1–3.3 Expected mean squares and method-of-moments variance-component estimates
contents.reason: SME-07 does not claim the balanced or unbalanced ANOVA variance estimators, their bias, or their boundary truncation; these are absent from the controlling plan.

contents.name: 1.1–1.4 Fixed-effects ANOVA decomposition and exact F test
contents.reason: The pair does not introduce one-way fixed-effects ANOVA or exact F inference; it uses only the random-effects covariance interface relevant to mixed models.

sources.title: Fan Li, STA610 Lecture 4 Notes: Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Inference for the Hierarchical Normal Model
sources.locator: PDF p. 2 for known-V GLS; pp. 4–5, §4.1, for REML as the likelihood of error contrasts. The complete 6-page note was inspected.
sources.reading_verification: Read the complete local extracted text at scratchpad/statistics-scaffolds-2026-10-11/sources/models-01/duke-sta610-lec4-mle-reml.txt and verified the current official PDF link from the Duke course page. In §4.1 the source writes C^T Y with C an n by n-p contrast-basis matrix; this orientation is dimensionally consistent and supports the corrected local K convention.

contents.name: 2.1 Fixed effects at known variance components are GLS
contents.support: The source identifies the known-covariance fixed-effect estimator as GLS; the assigned theorem proves its unbiasedness, covariance, and BLUE property.

contents.name: 4.1 General REML error-contrast likelihood
contents.support: The source forms contrasts C^T Y with C^T X=0 so the fixed effect cancels. The local definition fixes a column basis K and proves its contrast covariance is positive definite.

contents.name: 3.1–3.3 Balanced one-way likelihood estimates and finite-sample bias
contents.reason: The controlling SME-07 plan defines REML but does not claim a balanced one-way closed form, an MLE bias formula, or an ANOVA equivalence.

contents.name: 5.2 Boundary likelihood-ratio inference for variance components
contents.reason: Variance-component boundary testing and likelihood-ratio calibration are not planned claims in the assigned pair and are not inferred from the REML definition.

contents.name: 1 Gaussian likelihood for the hierarchical normal model
contents.support: The note writes the likelihood for a multivariate-normal response using its covariance determinant and quadratic form. The local theorem proves the general nondegenerate Gaussian density from the scalar normal density, a Cholesky factor, and the linear change-of-variables theorem.

contents.name: 4.1–4.2 REML error contrasts and contrast-coordinate choice
contents.support: Section 4.1 defines REML through linear combinations annihilating the fixed-effect design; §4.2 notes in the balanced case that the contrast-space projection does not depend on the chosen contrast coordinates. The local proof establishes the general basis-change density factor for every full-rank design.

contents.name: 4.1 General REML error-contrast law
contents.support: The treatment defines REML through Gaussian error contrasts annihilating the fixed-effect design. The local lemma proves from the projection definition of the multivariate normal law that K^TY is Gaussian with covariance K^TVK, including singular contrast covariance.

sources.title: Fan Li, STA610 Lecture 5 Notes: Estimation of Group Effects
sources.locator: PDF pp. 8–10, §§4.2–4.5, for the random-groups BLUP and empirical-BLUP statements; the complete 11-page note was inspected.
sources.reading_verification: Read the complete local extracted text at scratchpad/statistics-scaffolds-2026-10-11/sources/models-01/duke-sta610-lec5-group-effects.txt. The note states the scalar balanced BLUP result but does not prove the general matrix result. Its empirical-BLUP warning is retained; fixed-groups risk and Bayesian sections are excluded.

contents.name: 4.2–4.4 Unbiased prediction and scalar balanced BLUP
contents.support: The source states the moment-based BLUP distinction and its unconditional unbiasedness. The assigned theorem supplies the full matrix proof, nuisance fixed-effect adjustment, and prediction-error covariance.

contents.name: 4.5 Empirical BLUP
contents.support: The source notes that empirical BLUP substitutes estimated variance components. The theorem remarks explicitly withhold the known-parameter covariance guarantee from this plug-in procedure.

contents.name: 3 Fixed-groups composite-risk argument and 5 Bayesian posterior interpretation
contents.reason: The owner direction excludes Bayesian and empirical-Bayes prerequisites, and the controlling plan does not request a prediction-risk comparison or a fixed-groups Stein argument.

sources.title: Fan Li, STA610 Lecture 6 Notes: Linear Mixed-Effects Models
sources.locator: PDF pp. 4–5 for the general matrix model; pp. 8–11 for marginal covariance and known-V GLS; pp. 13–15 for random-slope and identifiability examples. The complete 16-page note was inspected.
sources.reading_verification: Read the complete local extracted text at scratchpad/statistics-scaffolds-2026-10-11/sources/models-01/duke-sta610-lec6-lme.txt. Its inverse-D shrinkage display requires nonsingular random-effect covariance and is not used; the local conditional-law proof handles singular G by a residual argument.

contents.name: 2 and 4.1 General matrix mixed model and marginal covariance
contents.support: The source supplies Xβ+Zb+ε notation and the design-role distinction; its covariance formula is independently proved by the local moment lemma.

contents.name: 4.1 Marginal covariance ZDZ^T plus residual covariance
contents.support: The source states the general matrix covariance identity; the local proof checks all cross terms from independence and makes no Gaussian assumption.

contents.name: 5.1 Generalized least squares for fixed effects
contents.support: The source gives the GLS formula and covariance under known marginal covariance; the local theorem uses whitening and the current fixed-design Gauss–Markov result.

contents.name: 7.1 Constant-within-group covariates and random-slope aliasing
contents.support: The source motivates the identifiability warning. The assigned counterexample independently computes two positive-definite covariance-parameter tuples with exactly equal two-visit V.

contents.name: 3 Model comparison, software fitting, and numerical output
contents.reason: Likelihood-ratio inference, fitting algorithms, and R output are not mathematical claims in this assigned pair.

sources.title: Fan Li, STA610 Lecture 7 Notes: The Longitudinal Linear Mixed Model
sources.locator: PDF pp. 3–8 for subject/visit indexing, random intercept and random slope structures; pp. 16–18 for missingness mechanisms and dropout. The complete 21-page note was inspected.
sources.reading_verification: Read the complete local extracted text at scratchpad/statistics-scaffolds-2026-10-11/sources/models-01/duke-sta610-lec7-longitudinal-lme.txt, including the missing-data definitions and the warning that model fit under MAR relies on a specified observation mechanism. No MAR ignorability theorem, causal interpretation, R procedure, or empirical trial estimate is imported.

contents.name: 2 Longitudinal LMM definition and subject–visit design
contents.support: The source specializes group indices to subjects and repeated visits; the local definition states actual time origins, observed rows, and the separate observation mechanism.

contents.name: 5.1–5.2 Random-intercept and random-intercept/slope covariance
contents.support: The source shows how random slopes create time-dependent covariance. The local result proves the general ZGZ^T+R identity.

contents.name: 9.1 Missingness mechanisms and monotone dropout
contents.support: The source defines MCAR, MAR, MNAR, and monotone dropout relative to observed and unobserved outcomes; the local definition states the probability-kernel convention explicitly.

contents.name: 9.2 Likelihood analysis under MAR
contents.support: The source makes MAR a separate missingness premise. The finite counterexample shows that a complete-data random-intercept covariance law does not impose that premise.

contents.name: 7 Randomized-trial treatment effects and 10 causal assumptions
contents.reason: The assigned pair is a model and covariance development, not a causal treatment-effect or missing-data ignorability theorem.

sources.title: Duchateau, Janssen, and Rowlands, Linear Mixed Models, Chapter 2: The Mixed Model Methodology
sources.locator: Full Chapter 2 text; inspected §§2.3.1–2.3.3, 2.4.1–2.4.3 and 2.5.1, including the text of Appendix D referenced by §2.4.3.
sources.reading_verification: Opened the complete public Chapter 2 full-text page and inspected the mixed-model matrix formulation, covariance derivation, error-contrast construction, BLUP discussion, and GLS formula at their exact section locators. The chapter uses a row-basis K with KY, whereas the assigned K^TY formula requires the transpose-compatible column-basis convention used locally. Its BLUP section is scalar and is not treated as a proof of the general matrix result.

contents.name: 2.3.1–2.3.3 Random/fixed effects and matrix mixed-model form
contents.support: The source states the fixed-plus-random matrix formulation and distinguishes its parameter roles; the local definition adds a model-contract and longitudinal observation specification.

contents.name: 2.4.1 Mixed-model marginal covariance
contents.support: The source derives the ZD(u)Z^T plus residual-covariance formula under independence; the local theorem retains the general residual matrix R.

contents.name: 2.4.2 Restricted maximum likelihood from error contrasts
contents.support: The source shows that full-rank linear combinations annihilating X have a law independent of fixed effects. Its row-basis KY dimensions differ from the plan's K^TY orientation; the local definition uses an n by n-p column basis and proves covariance nonsingularity.

contents.name: 2.4.3 Best linear unbiased prediction of random effects
contents.support: The source gives the scalar normal-model prediction route. The local theorem proves the matrix BLUP and its prediction-error covariance from moment assumptions.

contents.name: 2.5.1 GLS fixed-effect estimate
contents.support: The source identifies the known-covariance GLS expression and its covariance; the local proof supplies the whitening and BLUE argument.

contents.name: 2.4 variance-component estimation and 2.5 inference procedures
contents.reason: The assigned plan does not claim ML optimization, ANOVA moment estimators, confidence intervals, or variance-component tests; only the error-contrast likelihood definition is retained.

contents.name: 2.4.2 Error contrasts, REML covariance, and Gaussian likelihood
contents.support: The section supplies the restricted Gaussian likelihood from error contrasts. It uses row-basis coordinates KY, while the local theorem and likelihood use the equivalent transpose-compatible column-basis convention K^TY; the local density theorem supplies the full Gaussian density argument.

contents.name: 2.4.2 Error-contrast basis and restricted likelihood
contents.support: The section treats full-rank contrasts that remove the fixed effects. The local change-of-basis proof supplies the determinant calculation showing that different bases of this contrast space change likelihood values only by a parameter-free factor.

contents.name: 2.4.2 Gaussian law of error contrasts
contents.support: The section derives REML from Gaussian linear combinations that remove the fixed effects. It uses row-basis KY; the local proof states the transpose-compatible column-basis K^TY and derives its multivariate-normal law directly.
